title: MongoDB Relationships and @DBRef
summary: Choose embedding or references and manage their save, delete and read behavior.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Mastering MongoDB Relationships in Spring Boot: @DBRef Annotation for Seamless Collection Linking!
Spring Data MongoDB: DBRef and document references

richText: Embedding and references
Embedding stores a child object inside its parent document. A reference stores a link to a separately stored document.
Choose embedding for small data that belongs to one parent and is usually read with it. One document write can update the parent and its embedded data together.
Choose references when entries have an independent lifecycle, are queried separately or would make the parent document grow without a practical bound.
The course stores journal entries separately. User holds a list of journal entry references through @DBRef.
@DBRef stores MongoDB database references. It resolves linked documents into Java objects when loading the parent. It does not create JPA relationships.
Save both documents explicitly
DBRef does not cascade saves. Saving User does not save a new JournalEntry automatically.
First save the entry. Then add the saved entry to User and save User. The saved entry has the ID needed for its reference.
These are two database writes. If the second write fails outside a transaction, the first saved document can remain without the user reference.
Deleting an entry also needs an explicit policy for its user reference. Deleting a user does not automatically delete its referenced entries.
Read cost and ownership
DBRef resolves eagerly by default. Lazy references defer loading until accessed. Lazy loading still performs database work.
Loading many referenced entries can increase database and network work. Prefer bounded reads and pagination for growing journals.
For a large journal, another design stores userId on each entry and queries entries by that ID. This avoids an ever-growing reference list on User.
A relationship does not establish permission. Read, update and delete operations must verify that the authenticated user owns the requested entry.
@DocumentReference is another Spring Data mapping option. Its default representation stores referenced IDs. It also requires explicit saves.
Choose your storage model from read and update patterns. Do not assume @OneToMany, JPA cascade rules or foreign-key enforcement apply to MongoDB.
